methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center study with very small sample and severe group imbalance. LAG3 I455hom group (n=6): 83% male, 33% CAR-T prior vs. T455hom (n=11): 36% male, 91% CAR-T prior. Extreme subgroup sizes with estimated HRs of 14-16 and CIs crossing null (0.82-403), indicating severe overfitting and statistical instability. No multiple comparison correction. Multivariable Cox modeling with limited power cannot adequately control confounding with such disparate baseline characteristics and small event counts.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Ultra-selected population (n=28 multi-drug resistant, mostly CAR-T refractory DLBCL). Clinical applicability severely limited. LoE 4 (tiny case series). Findings non-generalizable to R/R DLBCL broadly.

reporting_quality.justification: Basic methods described but incomplete detail on genotyping validation, QC procedures. No data or code sharing. Acknowledgment of imbalances present but inadequate in methods section prior to results.

novelty_literature.justification: Replication in new treatment context (glofitamab vs. CAR-T) of previously studied SNP; minimal novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: Organized but presentation emphasizes dramatic findings (HR 14-16) without adequate front-loading of caveats. Extensive limitations section appropriately cautious but comes after results already presented with impact.

key_strengths: Explores potentially important immune checkpoint polymorphism in new therapeutic context
Attempts multivariate analysis to adjust for confounders
key_concerns: Critically small sample (n=28) divided into tiny subgroups (n=6-11) with severe baseline imbalance (sex, prior therapy)
HR estimates (14-16) with 95% CIs crossing null (0.82-403) are statistically unstable and indicate overfitting
Study population so highly selected (75% CAR-T refractory, multi-drug resistant) that findings have no generalizable clinical value
Imbalances between subgroups (83% vs. 36% male, 33% vs. 91% CAR-T) inadequately controlled
Method section does not adequately foreground imbalance concern; results presentation emphasizes dramatic but unstable HRs
chief_reviewer.rationale: This extremely preliminary exploratory study in a tiny, severely imbalanced, ultra-selected population reports dramatic findings (HR 14-16) with statistical instability (CIs crossing null). Rejection at tier 4 is appropriate. If resubmitted, authors must: (1) remove or contextualize HR presentations with clear 'overfitting risk' language, (2) substantially temper all conclusions, (3) reframe as ultra-preliminary proof-of-concept requiring validation in larger, balanced cohorts, or (4) revise methodology fundamentally.
